column8: Thu 19 Nov: 2.3 or 3c, Q174-001's slot: the court's own reasoning is the deletion test (the lead works as if there were no rubber at the other end, para 44, checked at LII today), matching NUMBERS 4 (VT at zero, all ten paid, one figure, $95,000); use this quote or Q174-001's, never both, one outside name per part; not in 3e beside rub out every pencil line; absorbs row 16.

Thu 19 Nov: 3e and Table 3 row 4: the same paragraph lists what the pencil lacked (no relation between the instruments, no reciprocal action, no parts used in common; checked at LII today), and the plan has two parts used in common, the late-2032 fund behind the 2033 payment, the bottom and the top (8w) and the extra Treasuries behind all ten (8a); corrects Q174-001's use and Q174-002's the parts never interact, and the AHA_REGISTER pencil candidate's its parts meet once at the move; absorbs row 3.

Thu 19 Nov: merged into Q181-002: the handle in common is the shared fund in the court's own image; its lesson (the court never asked what breaks with the handle; 8w: $4,589 on the top at worst with cash waiting earning nothing, nothing short at today's market rates) travels with row 2.

Thu 19 Nov: store, a wording guard: IBTM does two jobs (TNA l.13) is not the court's watch key, one instrument doing double duty, but separate lots bought on separate dates (CANON A24, D2); never say the court would have patented any part of the plan.

Thu 19 Nov: store; corrects Q174-002's reading that the law calls any sequence no invention: the same paragraph allows parts working successively, so the order point is told as order of use against order of purchase (row 6), never order as such.

Thu 19 Nov: 2.3 beside the order-of-purchase reserve, one clause with Q174-002: the court meant the order of use, the plan's is an order of claim on scarce money, shown with a short deposit, never the central case; fix: about three-quarters smaller only with at today's rates (WORDS, 8u), and what is left is split between the fund and VT, the fund taking the larger part (AHA_REGISTER fix), never and then the shares; Curtis unread.

Thu 19 Nov: merged into Q181-022: claim a good idea, never a new one, is the same writers' stance (the plan's merit is its fit to Laura, not novelty); low fees and one broker as workmanship add nothing the report can say.

Thu 19 Nov: store, a guard checked at LII today: Strong, Davis and Bradley dissented on the pencil, so never the Court unanimously ruled; the dissent gives no reasons, so nothing more is drawn from it.

Thu 19 Nov: merged into Q174-012 (Lejeune's test of verification), as the card itself says; the same fix applies: Table 1 is the WInS book scaled, not her record, so never Table 1's CUSIPs as what makes a figure ink.
Thu 19 Nov: merged into Q65-032 (custody at one broker, 8t): the court's one-rod convenience is decoration on a sized exposure; above SIPC's $500,000 the history is delay, not loss.

Thu 19 Nov: merged into Q174-001: Hailes is the rule the pencil case applied, each part working out its own effect, the same point as TNA l.15's dedicated instrument; the pooled extra Treasuries are the exception (Q181-002).

Thu 19 Nov: store; tenants in common is the property-law image for CANON D2's separate lots in one fund (each lot takes its own share of an early end); say it plainly, separate lots, and keep 8w part C beside it: the 2033 lot's loss still reaches the 2036 payment through the pool.
Thu 19 Nov: merged into Q181-014: mere adding together, not a vital union, is the same point as two and two make only four, which says it better.

Thu 19 Nov: 3d's reserves or a writers' rule, one clause at most: a promise should fail the test a patent must pass, so her side of the sum is exact (SD-1) and the parts can be shown (Q159-020); never a case name in Laura's words, and never a co-sponsor holding Table 1 (the WInS book, not her record; Q174-012); absorbs row 13.

Thu 19 Nov: store, a word guard: the same Court disowned combination and aggregation as tests in 1950, so the report never uses either as a label and says each part does its own job; qualifies Q174-001's aggregation quote (history, not today's law); absorbs row 17.
Thu 19 Nov: merged into Q181-001: a second deletion test in the Court's words (the heater would work as well in tandem); one deletion-test quote per report.
Thu 19 Nov: merged into Q181-015: never claim synergy between the plan's parts is the same word guard.
Thu 19 Nov: merged into Q181-019: KSR quotes Sakraida's old elements performing their known functions; the striking result (IPS l.11's none) rides with row 19 or row 14.

Thu 19 Nov: the parallel's present-day footing if the pencil turn is used: KSR's predictable results, not aggregation, so a promise needs what a patent is refused; pairs with row 14, one of the two in prose; foreseeable to a skilled person is not money on a date, so the shape carries, not the content; absorbs row 18.

Thu 19 Nov: store, a correction to Q174 idea 1(c) and Q174-002's note (the one interaction, the 2031 move): the move is two old operations in sequence, half of VT sold and more of the late-2032 fund bought, a dependence of size (VT's value that day), not of operation.

Thu 19 Nov: merged into Q181-022: its honest corollary travels there (a dedicated Treasury portfolio is textbook, Q1c-029, so the plan is obvious to a bond desk and new only against IPS l.9's first instinct); Adams unread, so never cite it.

Thu 19 Nov: a frame for 3.0's writers, no case name: patent law ignores the reason, while the plan stands on its reason for one client (IPS l.9; CANON A3), so the report claims a good fit, never a new idea; absorbs rows 7 and 21; fix: drop which is why Wharton scores Client Knowledge apart, an unsupported claim about the rubric.

Thu 19 Nov: merged into Q181-026 (the ties run one way); its fix travels: a smaller deposit reaches the ten once it is more than about three-quarters smaller at today's rates (8u), so never never the ten.

Thu 19 Nov: store, the correction behind the card's What the deeper reading changed: modern patent law dropped aggregation and synergy as tests (Stratoflex, read through quotations), so the parallel rests on KSR (row 19); fix: read MPEP 2173.05(k) at uspto.gov before citing it (a reproduction only so far).
Thu 19 Nov: store; a synthesis of three submitted lines (IPS l.9, l.11, TNA l.23) that adds only the patent frame; a counterbalance works by not moving with her income, never a natural hedge.

Thu 19 Nov: 2.3, the cause the order-of-purchase reserve lacked: each part's size depends only on parts bought before it, so a smaller deposit shrinks the building money and no fall in one part can force a sale of another (IPS l.17); fix: at today's rates and only to about three-quarters smaller (8u: beyond that, or with a missed deposit, the payments are reached), what is left is split with the fund taking the larger part, and two ties run sideways (the shared fund, the pooled extra Treasuries); Keel's mapping; absorbs row 23.

Thu 19 Nov: 3e reserve beside Table 3 row 4, 8w part C checked: an early end of the late-2032 fund on 1 Jan 2031 with cash waiting earning nothing leaves the ten $1,827 short, landing on 2036 where the extra Treasuries bind, and all ten are paid at today's market rates; shows the shared part concretely, but 3e prose keeps 8w's one figure, $4,589 on the top; no probability for an early end.

Thu 19 Nov: 2.2, one clause beside GOLDMINE 27: Simon's watchmakers give the three dated steps a cause any reader sees (each step finishes a stable form) and a prediction NUMBERS confirms (8u: no yield move breaks the ten after January 2028; section 4: after the move markets change neither end); the first plan as Tempus matches 8s (one date, 1 Jan 2033), never in 3f and never its reason (IPS l.9, CANON A3); absorbs row 29.
Thu 19 Nov: merged into Q181-028: the prediction half of the watchmakers travels with it; finished parts are not wholly safe here (a US default, a fund event, 8w), which Simon's are.

Thu 19 Nov: store, the accurate word for notes and writers, nearly decomposable (strong ties inside each promise, weak ties through the shared fund and the pool), replacing Q174-001 and Q174-002's the parts never interact; never in the report.

Thu 19 Nov: 3e accuracy, a correction to Q165-024: the one-off Bill needed only a majority in law but passed third reading 438 to 20, above two-thirds of 650 (434, Keel arithmetic); never a simple majority beat a two-thirds rule if the Act's story is told.

Thu 19 Nov: 3c or 3e store: the reviewers found the only substantive difference was that the Bill named polling day; the use is why the report names each step's date, January 2031 being the register's step (NUMBERS 8r), never the IPS's words (Before you meet co-sponsors in 2031); the break (nobody fears Laura's dates; 1 Apr or 1 Jul 2031 still states $115,000) limits it to when co-sponsors can start counting.

Thu 19 Nov: store; the reviewers' repair (exits each recognised by a fact and a date) resembles IPS l.17 read through Table 3, but Table 3's dates are Keel's reading (row 17) and their exits stay votes.
Thu 19 Nov: store; the 2019 Act wore s.2's label without amending the Act; its use (only her own deposit can carry a market fall in) is row 19's, merged into Q134-039.

Thu 19 Nov: 3e, a better source for Q165-026's line (a rule is only as strong as what holds it): the reviewers' own words about the Act (No Parliament can bind its successor; in practice it did not do so) replace Elster's Polish footnote; IPS l.17 is a letter and no stated figure rests on it; absorbs row 10.
Thu 19 Nov: merged into Q183-021 (who holds the keys); Butler's line is contested in the same report (Letwin, para 33), so never alone.

Thu 19 Nov: merged into Q183-022: an override was always contemplated, as Laura's freedom to rewrite is; it reaches a step not yet taken, never what a held Treasury pays, which row 22 sets out by date.

Thu 19 Nov: merged into Q165-004 (a Treasury pays on its date with nobody watching): the reviewers' default expectation may join it as a phrase, said plainly, never as a slogan flip against a default outcome.

Thu 19 Nov: store; the Act met its immediate aim, a clear commitment to the smaller partner, which explains Q165-025's one full term; co-sponsors as that partner is a weak map, and never implies they distrust Laura (case l.114).
Thu 19 Nov: merged into Q183-005; its guard travels: say flawed in several respects, never the Act failed without naming the aim it met.

Thu 19 Nov: 3e, outside support for Q109-033 (two lists): naming some exits in statute undermined the shared understanding of the rest, so two named reasons must not read as nothing else is acted on; Table 3 acts on an early fund end or a debt-limit deadline without calling either a reason (CANON A34).
Thu 19 Nov: store; a list of exits says nothing about powers outside it (prorogation, Miller), which is Table 3's job; Miller read in the press summary only.

Thu 19 Nov: store, and a small correction to Q165-023: the Act also allowed a bounded two-month delay, so exactly two ways out is true of early elections only; Table 3 row 5's day-by-day delay is Keel's, not the IPS's.
Thu 19 Nov: store; a rule's dated review re-decides it, while Laura's dated steps are purchases nothing re-decides; no report job beyond row 22.
Thu 19 Nov: store; the repeal kept a date and dropped the list, a neat fact behind 3e's the rule is not what keeps the figures, but 3e has room for one Act clause and rows 5 and 22 carry it better.
Thu 19 Nov: merged into Q7b-039 (reason 1 is her own deposit), which said so on 14 Nov; Q165-023's critique and Q165-024's use (Laura's reasons are not choices) need this fix.

Thu 19 Nov: 3e and Table 3 row 1 wording guard, checked against CANON A34 and ASK_HUMANS (Wed 11 Nov 19:50): nothing received by 31 March 2028 is Keel's reading, so say we read a missed deposit as nothing received by 31 March 2028, never the IPS closes the exit then; the same fix applies to Q165-024's rater note, Q7b-039 and the AHA_REGISTER Fixed-term Parliaments candidate.

Thu 19 Nov: merged into Q2a-024 (the missed deposit sized, NUMBERS 5: $2,287 unbought, $3,016 at today's market rates, $57,455 if cash waiting earns nothing, each with its basis); its new line, before any range is stated in place of before anyone relies on a figure, corrects Q165-024 and Q7b-039.

Thu 19 Nov: merged into Q134-039 (the plan relies on her career once, through the deposit); its guard travels: never a fall in the market cannot change the plan without the deposit beside it (CONCEIT l.472).

Thu 19 Nov: store; the want and cannot doors sharpen, not overturn, Q7b-033: the exit opens on a fact (no money received) whatever its cause; never present Laura choosing not to deposit as a plan case, since the case says she will contribute (l.43).
Thu 19 Nov: store; IPS l.17's we binds the adviser and Laura can release it, so the only key neither holds is the issuer's; Keel's reading, carried in prose by row 22; absorbs row 6.

Thu 19 Nov: 3e or 3c, the dated version of Q165-025 and Q165-026: most of each payment owned from January 2027, the ten, the extra Treasuries and the bottom from January 2028, the top from the move (CONCEIT, NUMBERS 4, 8r), the steps and the two reasons bound only by the letter, so a rewrite reaches only what is not yet stated; owning does not stop a sale (CANON A8); absorbs row 7.

Thu 19 Nov: 3e clause or Table 3 row 3's note beside Q15-024: Congress has acted 78 separate times since 1960 (Treasury's page, checked today; the count is undated), and the weakness that undid the Act, a rule set aside when it bites, is what keeps Treasuries paying; it explains why reason 2 is remote, never why a payment is safe (H3-013); never Congress will always raise it.

Thu 19 Nov: store; Norway's amendment rule binds because the hands that change it are not today's hands, as only the issuer sets what a held Treasury pays; Laura can still sell, and the text is the Storting's unofficial translation.

Thu 19 Nov: 3c, the source under the division: Hirschman's essay read whole sets three conditions (another way round, people caught, money to finish), firmer ground than Q172-014's mechanism quoted through his critic; once the necessary funds were secured is Hirschman's summary of Sawyer, and never secured for any part of her range.

Thu 19 Nov: merged into Q187-027: the case's rules (a fixed $50,000; no outside funding, l.90-92, checked) remove conditions one and three for the payments, the half of the division the synthesis carries.

Thu 19 Nov: 3c or 3d: a co-sponsor misled by a figure is not caught and can leave (case l.114-115, checked), so Hirschman's own condition explains the case's warning about promising more than she can give; the link is Keel's.
Thu 19 Nov: store; the December 2032 condition is the co-sponsors' (SD-3) and Hirschman names its price; her flexibility's third use is not sized (CANON A31), so never a bounded rescue with a figure.
Thu 19 Nov: store or a 3c reserve: Hirschman's timing rule (trouble should not show too early) is what the case forbids for her figure (l.114); it applies to the building's own difficulties only.

Thu 19 Nov: 3c or 3d reserve: Hirschman's cure for early trouble is a backer with a long-term commitment, and by January 2028 all ten years of operations to 2042 are owned (8u), so the building's real cost showing early cannot end the residency's running money; early means at the 2031 meetings, never a figure stated before them.

Thu 19 Nov: corrects Q172-014's framing (the plan takes Hirschman's side for the building): Hirschman called the Hand a matter of luck to be narrowly circumscribed, never advice to rely on ignorance, so refusing it for the promises is on his side; the book's typically and the article differ (card Gaps).

Thu 19 Nov: 3e, one clause: Hirschman wanted the crutch dropped once planners can tell acceptable from non-acceptable risk, and IPS l.19 with TNA l.23 draw that line in the open (risk in VT, none in the promises); not 3f, and one outside name per part.

Thu 19 Nov: store; designing to a budget is routine for an architect, so no limit needs hiding; Keel's application (Hirschman contrasted countries), and the case asks for no design advice (l.164-165).
Thu 19 Nov: store: Q172-012's survivor point in Hirschman's own words (survival is not vindication); a reason her flexibility is a limit, not a promise to finish whatever it costs.

Thu 19 Nov: 3d writers' rule: fundraising's usual lever is a magnifying glass for benefits, and Laura's words lead with a figure owned in Treasuries, so they may be hopeful about art, never about money; no outside name in Laura's words.
Thu 19 Nov: store, a writer's caution for 3f (told as it happened, never as foresight), already standing order 21's before, trigger, after; no outside name in 3f (panel 4).
Thu 19 Nov: merged into Q187-027: creativity cannot possibly save the day is the money side of the division (no creativity changes what a Treasury pays), already Q172-014's use.

Thu 19 Nov: 3b or 3e limit, checked today in arXiv draft 4.3's Table 2 (18 buildings, 28% benevolent, p = 0.048; all 327 projects 22%, 3.5 to 1): corrects Q172-014's break (about one project in five) for buildings to about one in four, 5 of 18 large public buildings; fix: name the sample and the draft, never mix with later versions' 80 percent and four to one.
Thu 19 Nov: merged into Q145-009 (low-balled works budgets, strategic misrepresentation); adds only the funding-contest cause; never cannot be bent or cannot move for a stated figure (NUMBERS 3).
Thu 19 Nov: merged into Q187-017; the authors themselves say it is not Hirschman's mechanism.

Thu 19 Nov: store; regulation fixes the outcome and lets cost float while a design budget fixes the money and lets the building float, so the parallel breaks under its own disanalogy; the case asks for no design advice (l.164-165); absorbs row 16.
Thu 19 Nov: store; fix: the plan arranges only the third condition (money to finish, her flexibility), not each; the other two are facts about a building.
Thu 19 Nov: store; Ika's 161 World Bank projects, abstract and opening only; a small building is where planning works, so the residency needs no ignorance to start.

Thu 19 Nov: store or a 3e clause: the plan takes no side in the Hiding Hand debate, since a building overrun is in no promise's break set (8u) and only her flexibility depends on the answer; two outside names, so notes only unless 3e has room.

Thu 19 Nov: 3b or 3e: the founder is the person escalation reaches first, and IPS l.15 (overruns named first for her flexibility) with l.17 (an overrun is not a reason) set that limit before she is caught; a 1976 role-play, so lean on the meta-analysis (row 22); founders as a rule, never Laura as irrational.

Thu 19 Nov: store, the evidence under row 21: responsibility, sunk costs and nearness to completion drive escalation (excerpts read, effect sizes not); all three will apply to her once the building is under way.

Thu 19 Nov: store: lock-in is the mechanism behind card Q5d's Laura's stage comes before every baseline (published overruns are measured from a later decision); two Dutch rail cases, abstract and conclusions only.

Thu 19 Nov: store; most overrun comes before construction, the window in which her flexibility is still in shares, which is 8q's joint risk (a share slump then a cost burst) already in 8u; Dutch transport, abstract only; supports Q172-031's watch.

Thu 19 Nov: 3c store: a design drawn to a top stated a year before the move would meet the shortfall after the architect is stuck (10.6% of house paths, NUMBERS 4, checked); fix: 8w has the bottom owned from January 2028 but stated only in 2031, so never suggest stating either end, to an architect or co-sponsors, before the 2031 meetings, and never advice on design (case l.164-165).
Thu 19 Nov: store: why Q172-031's building watch is safe in this plan (an early signal changes nothing the IPS fixes); a watch, never a third reason to change (IPS l.17).

Thu 19 Nov: 3c, the card's strongest: Hirschman's own three conditions hold for the building and fail for the promises, by the case's rules for the payments and by the co-sponsors' freedom to leave for a stated figure, and the plan fixes the third (her flexibility) before anyone is caught; supersedes Q172-014's division, whose break becomes about one building in four (row 14); absorbs rows 2 and 13.

Thu 19 Nov: store, for the conceit file: the Hiding Hand hides a difficulty so people start, pencil and ink hides nothing and waits; 3c's one turn is already two inkings, two dates, so at most a plain clause, never a second turn.
